issue.title: Make sure that Channel operations are run in order

repository.name: playframework
repository.description: The Community Maintained High Velocity Web Framework For Java and Scala.

issue.body:
Introduce a SequentialRunner class to assist with running operations in order. Use this class to ensure that operations within the Channel objects returned by Concurrent.broadcast and Concurrent.unicast execute their operations sequentially.

This change _may_ fix a race condition in Play's WebSocket code (see #2646), but this hasn't been verified.

issue.title: Ensure that a keystore intended for a keymanager has private keys

repository.name: playframework
repository.description: The Community Maintained High Velocity Web Framework For Java and Scala.

issue.body:
When using client authentication, the key store must contain private keys.  JSSE does not do a very good job at communicating this, and so this patch iterates through the key manager's keystore and logs warnings if an entry is found without a private key, and logs an error if no private key is found. 

It does not throw exceptions or terminate early, as the TLS handshake will still work fine if even if the keystore is misconfigured if the server does not use client authentication.

body: Ok, doing an analysis of all build failures, I've found that this doesn't just impact Java WebSockets, it impacts Scala WebSockets too.  I'm therefore thinking that it's not the server side implementation, as I can't see how that could cause this, rather it's the test client.

repository.name: playframework
repository.description: The Community Maintained High Velocity Web Framework For Java and Scala.

body:
@hepin1989 You were right, this was caused by that issue.

The problem happens when the server accepts a connection, and then immediately sends a message.  Under some circumstances, this message could well end up being part of the first selector read.

I managed to produce by ensuring that Netty only used one worker thread, and putting a Thread.sleep after initiating the handshake.  This meant on the next read, it read both the handshake response, and the first (and in fact second and third) messages, and all those messages were lost.  I then upgrade to Netty 3.9.3, and the problem was fixed.

Good news is, this is only in the Netty WebSocket client, so this doesn't affect Play's server side WebSocket handling.  I've merged #3298 to fix.
